# Separator

A line between groups.

## When to use it

**In Dense data:** Groups toolbar actions.

- **Use it when:** Separating groups that spacing alone does not separate.
- **Not when:** Decoration between every item: spacing is quieter.

Instead:

- [Card](./card.md): A container, when groups need a boundary.

## How Dense data uses it

<div class="odv-grid two"><div class="odv-dd"><div class="stage"><div class="odv-eyebrow">Between page sections</div><div style="margin-top:6px"><b style="color:var(--color-status-success)">Use</b> space.gap.section and a hairline</div><div><b style="color:var(--color-status-danger)">Not</b> A card around every section</div></div><div class="cap">Lines separate without taking room from the data.</div></div></div>

## Words

- Lead with the object, then the state: "Alert 2041 contained."
- Use numbers, not words for numbers.
- One verb per button. No "please", no exclamation marks.
- Use: Investigate, Filter, Assign, Escalated, Resolved. Avoid: Oops, Awesome, Please, Simply.

The labels components use, from the voice tokens:

- `content.action.commit`: Save
- `content.action.cancel`: Cancel
- `content.action.destroy`: Delete
- `content.action.retry`: Retry
- `content.action.empty-action`: Change filters

See [Voice and tone](../voice.md) for the whole voice.

## Use it in code

```bash
npx open-ds add separator
```

The component reads only component keys and semantic tokens, so it follows the brand and mode on `<html>`.

## Tokens it reads

Separator reads 1 tokens of its own, each an alias of a semantic token. Each row is one part: its own token, the semantic it aliases, and the value it ends at. Change a semantic and every component that reads it follows; override one of Separator's tokens to change Separator alone.
